question: How do we resolve the gap between +47% Oct sales and a breached $29.25 stop in Stage 4 without hedging?

epigraph.quote: When the facts change or your hard stop breaks, you do not move the stop lower to protect your ego. You take the loss cleanly, move to cash, and protect your capital for the next Stage 2 leader.
epigraph.author: Portfolio Risk Discipline Maxim

web_blocks.html: Putting Chapters 1 through 8 side by side forces a clean, unhedged decision. ASE's top-line momentum is real. LEAP sales are scaling above $4.0 billion in FY2026, ATM gross margin hit 30.6% in Q3, and October sales rose +47.1% YoY to NT$88,615 million [1, 3, 27]. Yet Pass 1 forensics uncovered -NT$115,929 million of 9M 2026 FCF, a +53.9% debt jump to NT$406,461 million, and 2027 CapEx guided above $11.5B [3, 28, 29]. Pass 2 valuation math then proved our reconciled $1.22 FY2027E EPS at a TSMC-capped 13.5x puts Base fair value at just $16.47 (-37.3% below CMP) [13, 20]. ASE also faces Nov 18 U.S. BIS AI export curbs, 25% top-client reliance, and rising 2027–2028 rivals [30, 33, 34, 37]. On Nov 20, 2026, shares fell -13.84% to $26.27, dropping into STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED) and breaking our $29.25 hard stop [14, 21, 22].

web_blocks.title: Two-sided institutional steelman: bull vs. bear

web_blocks.html: Before executing our exit and rejection verdicts, we test the strongest version of both the bull and bear arguments. Neither side is trivial, yet valuation math and risk rules settle the tie.

web_blocks.caption: Two-Sided Institutional Steelman: Bull Thesis vs. Bear / Skeptic Thesis (Nov 20, 2026)
rows: AI Packaging Demand
LEAP >$4B in FY26, October ATM +57.7% YoY, and full-process CoWoS + CPO provide multi-year AI growth [3, 27].
Nov 18 BIS export rules cloud 2H27 orders while TSMC doubles internal CoWoS and Intel EMIB-T + Amkor Arizona win share [33, 34, 37].
Demand is strong today, but BIS friction and 2027–2028 capacity additions erode OSAT scarcity pricing.
Cash Flow & Balance Sheet
Customer deposits (Note 37(e), NT$109.2B other LT liabilities) co-fund CapEx and Q3 CFO hit NT$50.5B [28, 30].
9M26 FCF is -NT$115.9B, debt jumped +53.9% to NT$406.5B, Q3 net interest hit NT$2.61B, and CFO guided 2027 CapEx above $11.5B [3, 28, 29].
Negative FCF and 6x higher interest expense leave zero balance-sheet cushion if utilization stalls.
Valuation & Peer Gravity
At $26.27, headline Finviz screens show 12.72x forward P/E (~$2.07 Street EPS)—half its 52W high valuation [13].
Reconciled FY27E P&L ($30.2B at 12.2% OPM) yields $1.22 EPS ($16.47 at 13.5x); TSMC trades at 13.81x with 32.67% ROIC vs. ASE's 10.28% [13, 20].
At 21.5x reconciled $1.22 EPS, $26.27 is expensive vs. both TSMC (13.81x) and Amkor (10.96x).
Tape & Stop Rule
1D RSI (30.48) and 4H RSI (24.52) are oversold after a -37.6% 1M flush with tiny 0.50% short float [13, 21].
STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED) on 2.13x volume, -23.7% below 200D SMA ($34.43), -10.2% below $29.25 prior stop, in a market Downtrend [14, 22].
Honoring the breached $29.25 stop is mandatory; hoping for a bounce in Stage 4 violates our risk ratchet.
web_blocks.takeaway: While ASE's LEAP growth is real, negative FCF of -NT$115.9B, a $16.47 Base fair value (-37.3% below CMP), and a Stage 4 break below $29.25 require action. We issue an unhedged EXIT_IMMEDIATELY call on held shares and a REJECTED verdict for new capital.

web_blocks.html: We do not hedge a breached, overvalued Stage 4 chart with a speculative "wait for support" label. With Base fair value at $16.47 and no verified support floor between $26.27 and the $13.35–$13.71 52-week low, new capital is explicitly REJECTED (TIER_0).

book_paragraphs: We have reached the moment of execution. Over nine chapters, we audited ASE Technology's factories, corrected the USI segment mix, uncovered -NT$115.9 billion of nine-month cash burn, logged a 54 percent jump in debt to NT$406.5 billion, weighed the November 18 BIS export rules, reconciled FY2027E EPS to $1.22 ($16.47 Base fair value at a TSMC-capped 13.5x multiple), and watched the stock breach our $29.25 stop to close at $26.27 in Stage 4.

Now comes the test that separates disciplined portfolio management from wishful thinking. When a stock drops 13.84 percent in one day and breaches your prior hard stop by nearly 10 percent, human psychology begs for an excuse to wait. You tell yourself October sales were up 47 percent, Street forward P/E looks like 12.7 times, and surely you should wait for a bounce to $29 before selling.

That impulse is how manageable 14 percent losses turn into portfolio-scarring 40 to 50 percent drawdowns. Remember what we promised in writing on November 13: if ASX closes below $29.25, we exit all 82 Schwab shares to preserve capital and avoid riding a Stage 4 slide toward the bear case. Today, the close is $26.27 on 2.13x volume, 23.7 percent below the 200-day moving average, inside a ten-distribution-day market Downtrend.

Therefore, our holding action is EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all 82 Schwab shares—executed at market open or via opening-session VWAP if ASX gaps below $25.75, so no limit price ever traps the position. At $26.27, those 82 shares are worth $2,154.14 against your $2,500.59 cost basis ($30.50 per share), locking in a small, contained loss of $346.45 (-13.85 percent) on a 2.87 percent portfolio weight. Better yet, your total net worth sits at $75,110.60 with 234.2 percent effective S&P 500 beta exposure, and nine positions—including ASX, TSM, SKHY, ANET, VRT, BE, DOCN, KORU, and OCNL—move in lockstep at 40.31 percent of net worth. Selling 82 shares of 3.04-beta ASX immediately cuts 8.72 percent of effective S&P exposure and lifts consolidated cash from $2,540.35 to $4,694.49.

What about new capital? We assign an unhedged REJECTED verdict (TIER_0, strategy bucket REJECTED) based on three explicit pillars: TREND, CASH_FLOW, and VALUATION. We refuse to hide behind a timid WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT label when the stock sits in Stage 4 with no verified chart floor between $26.27 and $13.35–$13.71, burns NT$115.9 billion of free cash flow across nine months, and carries an expected value of just $17.44 (-33.6 percent below CMP). Moving ASX from the active Shortlist to the Discarded bench keeps our pipeline honest.

Where should the $2,154.14 in freed proceeds and $2,540.35 of existing cash go tomorrow morning? Our 100%-reconciled capital redeployment plan allocates 100 percent to USD cash and Treasury bills. Even though two quality Stage 2 names appear on our radar—Shortlist healthcare compounder AbbVie (ABBV) at $286.20 and outside value-software name Teradata (TDC) at $35.45—both sit slightly above their support buy zones ($277.05–$285.49 for ABBV and $32.11–$34.54 for TDC) during an active S&P 500 Downtrend where only 34.5 percent of stocks hold above their 50-day averages.

Holding 100 percent of marginal cash in T-bills is not passivity; it is active risk control. It protects your $4,694.49 liquidity pool while the semiconductor sector finishes its Stage 4 digestion, and positions you to step into true Stage 2 leaders only when index breadth heals back above 50 percent and distribution days subside.

book_subsections.title: Why Honoring the $29.25 Stop Beats Hoping for a Bounce
paragraphs: Every trader remembers the one time they sold at the bottom right before a two-day bounce, and forgets the ten times a Stage 4 stock kept sliding from $26 toward $12. Notice why the probability math favors exiting immediately at market open (even on a gap below $25.75): short interest is just 0.50 percent of float, so there are no trapped shorts forced to cover on a bounce, while 4H RSI sits at 24.52 under falling 10-week and 30-week averages.

More importantly, our reconciled valuation puts Base fair value at $16.47 (-37.3 percent below $26.27), probability-weighted expected value at $17.44 (-33.6 percent), and our Amkor-parity stress test at $11.55 (stressed expected value $14.98, or -43.0 percent). Exiting all 82 shares now eliminates open-ended downside and frees $2,154.14 of clean cash.

book_subsections.title: Conditions Required to Ever Re-Underwrite ASX From Discarded
paragraphs: A REJECTED verdict is a disciplined boundary, not a blind grudge against ASE Technology's engineers. ASE remains the global OSAT leader with 30.6 percent ATM gross margins and a genuine LEAP AI packaging franchise. If you want to know when this name could ever earn a fresh look, watch three strict milestones over the next two to four quarters.

First, ASX must stop falling and carve out a multi-month Stage 1 horizontal base—likely inside our $14.00 to $16.00 value watch band (11.5x to 13.1x reconciled $1.22 EPS, just above the $13.35–$13.71 52-week low)—followed by a high-volume Stage 2 reclaim of its 30-week and 200-day moving averages. Second, quarterly filings must show free cash flow turning cleanly positive as 2026–2027 cleanrooms fill up and debt growth stops. Third, management must prove on earnings calls that U.S. BIS export licensing and TSMC/Amkor/Intel competition are not eroding 2027 LEAP margins. Until all three appear in filings and on the tape, keep your capital safely in USD cash.

book_subsections.title: Portfolio Cluster Math: Why Exiting 82 Shares Strengthens the Whole Book
paragraphs: Zooming out from ASX as a single ticker to your total consolidated portfolio highlights why an immediate exit makes even more sense at the portfolio level. Across Schwab and Robinhood, total net worth stands at $75,110.60, yet high-beta equities, leveraged ETFs, and options push effective S&P 500 exposure to $175,884.92—or 234.2 percent of equity. Worse, nine of your holdings—including ANET, OCNL, ASX, BE, DOCN, KORU, SKHY, TSM, and VRT—exhibit 1-year return correlations above 0.65 and behave like a single 40.31 percent bet.

Exiting all 82 Schwab shares of ASX at $26.27 removes $2,154.14 of capital—and $6,548.59 of beta-adjusted market exposure—from that crowded cluster in a single click. Combined with $2,540.35 of existing cash, your USD cash buffer expands by 85 percent to $4,694.49 while Stage 2 healthcare and software comparators ABBV and TDC remain monitored at zero percent until market breadth recovers.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A good stop rule is worthless if you renegotiate it—or block it with a tight limit order—the morning after it triggers. Selling all 82 ASX shares immediately, moving ASX to Discarded, and holding 100% of freed proceeds in USD cash turns a broken, overvalued Stage 4 trade into fresh dry powder.
